summary: Configured a persistent routed WireGuard wg01 tunnel between node1 and node2 for 192.168.10.0/24 (lan-a) and 192.168.20.0/24 (lan-b). Node3 serves TCP/8080, and node4 receives HTTP 200 through the tunnel. Source addresses remain unchanged, no NAT is configured, and default-deny forwarding permits only new node4-to-node3 TCP/8080 connections. All four nodes were restarted individually and fully recovered.
actions_performed: Configured and saved VyOS LAN addresses, wg01 peers, remote-LAN routes, and stateful forwarding policy.
Configured persistent LAN addresses and routes on node3 and node4.
Installed and enabled the node3 application service bound to 192.168.10.10:8080.
Verified successful HTTP traffic, WireGuard transfer, original client source address, and absence of NAT.
Verified TCP/8081 and reverse cross-LAN ICMP are blocked; removed the temporary test listener.
Safely restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Routed wg01 tunnel between lan-a and lan-b without address translation
evidence.summary: Both gateways show recovered wg01 interfaces, remote-LAN routes through wg01, active transfer counters, exact forwarding rules, and no NAT configuration.

evidence.requirement: node4 reaches the node3 TCP/8080 application through the tunnel
evidence.summary: node4 routes from 192.168.20.10 via its LAN gateway and receives HTTP 200 from 192.168.10.10; node3 logs the unchanged 192.168.20.10 source and both gateway permit counters increase.

evidence.requirement: Only the application path permits new cross-LAN connections
evidence.summary: A live TCP/8081 listener was reachable locally but timed out from node4 and incremented node2's default-drop counter. Reverse cross-LAN ICMP also failed and incremented node1's default-drop counter. The temporary listener was removed while TCP/8080 remained active.
